sentences.en: In July 2020, my grandfather was living in a care facility in Texas, and I was living pretty far away from him.
sentences.zh: 2020年7月，我的祖父住在得克萨斯州的一家护理机构里，而我住得离他相当远。

sentences.en: Our family found out that he'd caught COVID, and from everything we'd been reading and hearing at the time, it seemed that his survival, as someone who's especially
sentences.zh: 我们家族发现他感染了新冠，根据我们当时阅读和听到的一切，作为一个特别

sentences.en: vulnerable, was pretty unlikely.
sentences.zh: 脆弱的人，他能存活下来的可能性微乎其微。

sentences.en: So we decided to drive halfway across the country to Texas, just so we could see him and possibly be able to say goodbye to him through a closed window.
sentences.zh: 所以我们决定开车横跨半个国家去得克萨斯州，只为了能见他一面，或许还能隔着紧闭的窗户跟他道个别。

sentences.en: He passed away from COVID on July 8th.
sentences.zh: 他于7月8日因新冠离世。

sentences.en: I was feeling an immense amount of guilt.
sentences.zh: 我当时感到无比的内疚。

sentences.en: I hadn't really been present at the end of his life, and I couldn't really do anything to change his situation.
sentences.zh: 在他生命的尽头，我并没有真正陪伴在左右，而且我也无法改变他的处境。

sentences.en: I decided that I wanted to stick around in Texas and wait for him to be cremated,
sentences.zh: 我决定留在得克萨斯州，等着他被火化，

sentences.en: because driving his ashes home personally felt like the most dignified thing I could do for him.
sentences.zh: 因为亲自把他的骨灰开车送回家，是我能为他做的最有尊严的事。

sentences.en: So one day, while I was waiting to receive the ashes, I was cooking lunch and listening to the On Being podcast by Krista Tippett.
sentences.zh: 所以有一天，在等待领取骨灰的时候，我一边做午饭，一边听着克里斯塔·蒂佩特主持的播客《On Being》。

sentences.en: Her guest was a family sciences researcher named Pauline Boss, who, in the 1970s, coined this term, ambiguous loss.
sentences.zh: 她的嘉宾是一位名叫宝琳·博斯的家庭科学研究员，她在20世纪70年代创造了“模棱两可的失去”这个词。

sentences.en: At its core, Boss's theory is about any loss whose nature is uncertain.
sentences.zh: 博斯的理论核心在于任何性质不确定的失去。

sentences.en: She challenges the traditional Kubler-Ross and Freudian theories of grief, which tell us that grief is a linear process, and that it has a prescribed endpoint.
sentences.zh: 她挑战了传统的库伯勒-罗斯和弗洛伊德的悲伤理论，这些理论告诉我们，悲伤是一个线性过程，并且有一个既定的终点。

sentences.en: What Boss is saying is, there's actually no timeline for mourning these losses.
sentences.zh: 博斯所说的是，实际上悼念这些失去并没有时间表。

sentences.en: They might not ever end, because that person could still be with us, physically or psychologically.
sentences.zh: 它们可能永远不会结束，因为这个人可能仍然在身体上或心理上陪伴着我们。

sentences.en: Ambiguous loss was a way to describe the reality that my family and I had been living for a decade.
sentences.zh: 模棱两可的失去，是描述我和家人十年来一直生活的现实的一种方式。

sentences.en: My grandfather had been physically far away, but even when he was near us, he felt absent.
sentences.zh: 我的祖父在身体上离得很远，但即使他在我们附近时，他也让人感觉缺席。

sentences.en: He had Alzheimer's.
sentences.zh: 他患有阿尔茨海默病。

sentences.en: He couldn't remember my face or name, and he could barely even remember my mom, his own daughter.
sentences.zh: 他记不清我的长相和名字，甚至几乎记不清我母亲——他自己的女儿。

sentences.en: Boss, who's 87 years old, has a new book out called The Myth of Closure.
sentences.zh: 现年87岁的博斯出了一本新书，名叫《终结的神话》。

sentences.en: I started talking to her last February.
sentences.zh: 我去年2月开始和她交谈。

sentences.en: At the time, she was still mourning the loss of her husband, who had died a few months earlier of a stroke.
sentences.zh: 当时，她仍在悼念几个月前因中风去世的丈夫。

sentences.en: She was still becoming accustomed to this new role of hers.
sentences.zh: 她还在适应自己这个新角色。

sentences.en: She was no longer a wife and caregiver, but a widow.
sentences.zh: 她不再是妻子和照顾者，而是一位寡妇。

sentences.en: Learning how to live without him and without their regular routines was something that she was struggling to do.
sentences.zh: 学习如何在没有他、没有他们常规生活的情况下生活，是她一直在努力做的事。

sentences.en: That sensation of discomfort and newness, I think, is something familiar to all of us.
sentences.zh: 我想，那种不适感和崭新感，是我们所有人都熟悉的。

sentences.en: When I first visited Pauline
sentences.zh: 当我5月下旬首次拜访宝琳·

sentences.en: Boss in late May, Minneapolis was on the cusp of fully reopening.
sentences.zh: 博斯时，明尼阿波利斯正处于全面重新开放的前夕。

sentences.en: Boss, who was 87, greeted me in her building's lobby wearing thick framed glasses, her light blonde hair short, and an Apple watch
sentences.zh: 87岁的博斯戴着粗框眼镜在她的公寓大堂迎接我，她那一头浅金色的短发十分利落，左手腕上

sentences.en: clasped on her left wriSt. She cautiously extended a hand toward me.
sentences.zh: 戴着一块 Apple Watch。她谨慎地向我伸出一只手。

sentences.en: Can we shake hands?
sentences.zh: 我们可以握手吗？

sentences.en: She asked, smiling.
sentences.zh: 她微笑着问。

sentences.en: Dare we?
sentences.zh: 我们敢吗？

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 我们握了。

sentences.en: The apartment was bright, with two walls of windows pouring sky into the space.
sentences.zh: 公寓采光很好，两面墙的窗户将天空的明亮倾泻进空间里。

sentences.en: Bookshelves were filled with works of sociology, psychology, and history.
sentences.zh: 书架上摆满了社会学、心理学和历史学著作。

sentences.en: A section was devoted primarily to Sigmund Freud, and another to Boss's hometown, New Glarus, Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分专门留给了西格蒙德·弗洛伊德，另一部分则留给了博斯的家乡威斯康星州新格拉鲁斯。

sentences.en: Out the window, the Mississippi River churned under bridges, past the tangle of downtown.
sentences.zh: 窗外，密西西比河在桥梁下方翻腾，流过市中心的错综复杂。

sentences.en: The view, however spectacular, was not the apartment's selling point.
sentences.zh: 然而，这景色再壮观，也不是这间公寓的卖点。

sentences.en: The elevators were.
sentences.zh: 电梯才是。

sentences.en: Boss, an emeritus professor of family social science, the study of families and close relationships, chose the place seven years ago
sentences.zh: 博斯是一位家庭社会学（研究家庭和亲密关系的学科）的名誉教授，她七年前选择这个地方，

sentences.en: because her husband's declining health had made it difficult for him to climb the stairs of their house near the University of Minnesota, where she taught.
sentences.zh: 是因为丈夫日渐衰弱的健康状况，使他很难爬她们在明尼苏达大学（她曾执教的地方）附近的房子的楼梯。

sentences.en: His decline was gradual.
sentences.zh: 他的身体衰退是逐渐发生的。

sentences.en: In 2000, he was using a cane.
sentences.zh: 2000年时，他还在用手杖。

sentences.en: By last year, when he was 88, rheumatoid arthritis had rendered him unable to walk.
sentences.zh: 到去年他88岁时，类风湿性关节炎已经让他无法行走了。

sentences.en: Vascular issues resulted in open wounds on his legs.
sentences.zh: 血管问题导致他腿部出现开放性伤口。

sentences.en: Despite his illness, the couple maintained a semblance of normalcy, entertaining guests, going for drives and attending the theater, until last year, when the
sentences.zh: 尽管患病，这对夫妇还是维持了一种常态感，招待客人、开车兜风并去看戏，直到去年，

sentences.en: pandemic isolated them in the apartment.
sentences.zh: 大流行将他们隔离在这间公寓里。

sentences.en: Then, their only visitors were home health aides.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，他们唯一的访客是家庭保健护理员。

sentences.en: Once they left,
sentences.zh: 他们离开后，

sentences.en: Boss would take care of her husband, changing the dressing on his bandages and administering his medications.
sentences.zh: 博斯就会照顾她的丈夫，为他的绷带换药并给他喂药。

sentences.en: It sneaks up on you, Boss said, of the burden of caregiving and its attendant emotional struggles.
sentences.zh: “它会悄悄找上门来，”博斯在谈到照顾病人的负担及其伴随的情感挣扎时说道。

sentences.en: She felt a range of contradictory feelings.
sentences.zh: 她感受到了各种矛盾的情绪。

sentences.en: Gratitude for their time together,
sentences.zh: 对他们共度时光的感激，

sentences.en: grief over the loss of their old rhythms, and anxiety at the inevitability of his death.
sentences.zh: 对失去旧日节奏的悲伤，以及对他的死亡不可避免的焦虑。

sentences.en: Boss was also confused about her role in their partnership.
sentences.zh: 博斯也对自己在伙伴关系中的角色感到迷茫。

sentences.en: Once solely his wife, she was now also his caregiver.
sentences.zh: 她曾经只是他的妻子，现在也是他的照顾者。

sentences.en: With her husband's drawn-out illness, Boss's life came to resemble the cases she'd spent her career studying.
sentences.zh: 随着丈夫久病不愈，博斯的生活变得像她职业生涯中一直在研究的那些案例。

sentences.en: Nearly 50 years ago, as a doctoral student in child development and family studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, she researched families with at least one member
sentences.zh: 大约50年前，作为威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校儿童发展与家庭研究专业的博士生，她研究了至少有一名成员

sentences.en: who was either physically or psychologically absent.
sentences.zh: 在身体上或心理上缺席的家庭。

sentences.en: Her initial studies in the 1970s focused on families in which fathers were too busy working to spend time with their children, and later on the wives of
sentences.zh: 她在20世纪70年代的初步研究重点是那些父亲忙于工作而没时间陪孩子的家庭，后来又转向了在越南战争中

sentences.en: fighter pilots who were missing in action during the Vietnam War.
sentences.zh: 失踪的战斗机飞行员的妻子们。

sentences.en: The fathers were psychologically absent, but physically present, while the fighter pilots were the reverse.
sentences.zh: 父亲们在心理上缺席，但在身体上在场，而战斗机飞行员则刚好相反。

sentences.en: Each situation created a sensation of limbo for family members, a lingering sense of grief over losses whose nature was uncertain.
sentences.zh: 每种情况都给家庭成员造成了一种处于悬而未决的感受，对性质不确定的失去产生了挥之不去的悲伤感。

sentences.en: Sometimes, as is in the case of a death accompanied by a body and a certificate, the scope of loss is relatively clear.
sentences.zh: 有时，正如伴随着尸体和死亡证明的死亡一样，失去的范围是相对明确的。

sentences.en: But in the cases Boss studied, losses lacked such authoritative certainty.
sentences.zh: 但在博斯研究的案例中，失去缺乏这种权威的确凿性。

sentences.en: There were often no bodies, and thus no rituals for mourning.
sentences.zh: 通常没有尸体，因此也没有哀悼的仪式。

sentences.en: Rather than being tied to a specific event, these losses frequently extended over many years, deepening each day in ways that grievers could not register.
sentences.zh: 这些失去往往不是与某个特定事件挂钩，而是延续多年，每天都在以悲伤者无法察觉的方式加深。

sentences.en: Could such experiences even be considered losses?
sentences.zh: 这样的经历甚至能被认为是一种失去吗？

sentences.en: Boss, observing how families spoke about their missing relatives, coined a term to define the unclear and often unacknowledged absences in their lives.
sentences.zh: 博斯通过观察家庭如何谈论他们失踪的亲人，创造了一个词来定义他们生活中模糊且常常未被承认的缺席。

sentences.en: Ambiguous loss.
sentences.zh: 模棱两可的失去。

sentences.en: Over the next several decades, Boss studied and provided therapy to the family members of Alzheimer's patients, as well as the relatives of people whose bodies were
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几十年里，博斯研究并为阿尔茨海默病患者的家属，以及在自然灾害或9·11事件中世贸中心大楼倒塌后

sentences.en: never recovered after natural disasters or in the collapse of the original World Trade Center on 9-11.
sentences.zh: 尸体从未被找回的人的亲属提供治疗。

sentences.en: Theirs were losses without conclusion in the traditional sense of the term, an experience of paradox, a simultaneous absence and presence that eluded resolution.
sentences.zh: 对他们而言，这是没有传统意义上终点的失去，是一种悖论的体验，一种无法解决的缺席与在场并存的状态。

sentences.en: Can you mourn someone whose body is present even if the mind isn't, or whose death is unconfirmed?
sentences.zh: 你能够悼念这样一个身体在场但心智不在，或者死因未经证实的人吗？

sentences.en: Can you grieve a foreclosed future?
sentences.zh: 你能为一个被提前切断的未来感到悲伤吗？

sentences.en: The concept, Boss maintains, is inclusive, encompassing a range of moderate to severe losses that we might not perceive as such.
sentences.zh: 博斯坚称，这个概念是包容性的，涵盖了一系列我们可能并未意识到的中度到重度的失去。

sentences.en: It can take many forms, often quotidian, an alcoholic parent who, when inebriated, becomes a
sentences.zh: 它可以采取多种形式，通常是日常的：一个酗酒的父母，清醒与否判若

sentences.en: different person, a divorced partner with whom your relationship is ruptured but not erased, a loved one with whom you've
sentences.zh: 两人；一个与你关系破裂但并未彻底抹去的离异伴侣；一个因移民而

sentences.en: lost contact through immigration, or a child you've given up for adoption.
sentences.zh: 失去联系的挚爱；或者一个你送去收养的孩子。

sentences.en: These experiences are an accumulation of heartbreaks that we cannot always recognize.
sentences.zh: 这些经历是无法总是被我们认清的心碎的累积。

sentences.en: Freudian notions of grieving have taught us that mourning is a process leading to detachment, a sort of closure.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德式的悲伤观念教导我们，哀悼是一个通往抽离的过程，是一种某种程度上的释怀。

sentences.en: Boss finds this model misleading, perilously bound up in the way Americans conceptualize themselves.
sentences.zh: 博斯发现这种模式具有误导性，危险地绑定了美国人自我概念化的方式。

sentences.en: In a new book published this month,
sentences.zh: 在本月出版的新书

sentences.en: The Myth of Closure, Ambiguous Loss in a Time of Pandemic and Change, she writes that the United
sentences.zh: 《终结的神话：大流行与变局时代模棱两可的失去》中，她写道，

sentences.en: States is a place that privileges narratives of self-sufficiency and rationality.
sentences.zh: 美国是一个崇尚自给自足和理性叙事的国度。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Kubler-Ross's linear five stages of grief model, which implies that if we work hard enough and follow certain
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·库伯勒-罗斯的线性悲伤五阶段模型暗示，如果我们足够努力并遵循某些

sentences.en: steps, we'll be able to get over our losses within a reasonable timeline, remains a popular mode of thinking.
sentences.zh: 步骤，我们就能在合理的时间内走出失去的阴影，这依然是一种流行的思维模式。

sentences.en: But Boss argues that many losses do not follow such models, and our reliance on them does not equip us to cope.
sentences.zh: 但博斯辩称，许多失去并不遵循这样的模式，我们对它们的依赖并没有让我们具备应对能力。

sentences.en: By contrast, ambiguous loss gives us a term with which to acknowledge the amorphous nature of its emotional wounding.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，模棱两可的失去给我们提供了一个词，用来承认其情感创伤的无形本质。

sentences.en: People are able to identify with this type of loss when they have language for it.
sentences.zh: 当人们有了描述这种失去的语言时，他们就能与之产生共鸣。

sentences.en: Whenever you bring it up to somebody, Boss told me, they go almost within five minutes to one of their own.
sentences.zh: 博斯告诉我：“无论你什么时候向别人提起它，他们在五分钟内几乎就会联想到自己的一次经历。”

sentences.en: Perhaps this is why Boss's work has had a resurgence of interest among researchers and journalists during the past two years, in the wake of the pandemic, George Floyd's
sentences.zh: 也许这就是为什么在大流行、乔治·弗洛伊德被

sentences.en: murder, and the January 6th attack on the U.S.
sentences.zh: 谋杀以及1月6日美国国会

sentences.en: Capitol.
sentences.zh: 山骚乱之后，在过去的两年里，研究人员和记者对博斯的工作重新燃起了兴趣。

sentences.en: In a time when the global community is grappling with questions of atmospheric grief, she has broadened her attention beyond the family, looking,
sentences.zh: 在这个全球社群正在艰难应对大范围弥漫的悲伤问题的时代，她将注意力扩展到了家庭之外，

sentences.en: along with her acolytes, out to questions of societal bereavement.
sentences.zh: 与她的追随者一同放眼于社会悲痛的问题。

sentences.en: This influence isn't sudden.
sentences.zh: 这种影响并非突然出现。

sentences.en: After the 1999 publication of Boss's seminal book, Ambiguous Loss, Learning to Live with Unresolved
sentences.zh: 在博斯于1999年出版的开创性著作《模棱两可的失去：学会与未解的

sentences.en: Grief, numerous scholars began building on her work.
sentences.zh: 悲伤共处》之后，许多学者开始在她的工作基础之上进行深入研究。

sentences.en: They published papers examining exile, foster care, and traumatic brain injury through the lens of her theory.
sentences.zh: 他们发表了论文，通过她的理论视角来审视流放、寄养和创伤性脑损伤。

sentences.en: Today, younger researchers have inquired whether urgent social and political issues—the loss of the world as we know it as a result of
sentences.zh: 今天，年轻的研究人员开始探究，当下的社会和政治问题——由于气候变化

sentences.zh: 而失去我们所知的世界，或是遭受持续种族暴力的令人窒息的悲痛——是否能够用她的理论来理解。

sentences.en: This reflects ambiguous losses, growing influence, and breadth as a tool to understand why and how we grieve.
sentences.zh: 这反映了模棱两可的失去日益增长的影响力，以及它作为理解我们为何以及如何悲伤的工具的广度。

sentences.en: Boss takes pleasure in mentoring young scholars and seeing them apply the theory in innovative and often surprising ways.
sentences.zh: 博斯乐于指导年轻学者，并看他们以创新且常常令人惊讶的方式应用这一理论。

sentences.zh: “对我而言，如果这个理论有用，我就会感到很高兴。”

sentences.en: Inspired in part by the queries, the myth of closure takes a sweeping look at racial unrest and the pandemic while refuting the idea that grief has a prescribed endpoint.
sentences.zh: 部分受到这些质询的启发，《终结的神话》对种族骚乱和大流行进行了宏观审视，同时反驳了悲伤有一个既定终点的观点。

sentences.en: In some regards, the book is a testament to the ways in which these researchers have pushed her thought in new directions, particularly on race.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这本书见证了这些研究人员如何将她的思想推向新的方向，特别是在种族问题上。

sentences.en: Now, after much thinking since that fateful Memorial Day when
sentences.zh: “现在，自从我的家乡明尼阿波利斯发生乔治·弗洛伊德被杀的那场宿命般的阵亡将士纪念日以来，经过了这么多的思考，

sentences.en: around the world, I have expanded my ideas about ambiguous loss, she writes.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的种种疑问，我已经扩展了我对模棱两可的失去的看法，”她写道。

sentences.en: It can happen to one person, one family, a local community, or the global community.
sentences.zh: 它可能发生在一个人、一个家庭、一个地方社群或全球社群身上。

sentences.en: The myth of closure is also her attempt to make sense of simultaneously unfolding catastrophes in her personal life and around the world.
sentences.zh: 《终结的神话》也是她试图理解个人生活中以及世界各地同时发生的灾难的一种尝试。

sentences.en: This is the first time I've raised ambiguous loss to a higher level regarding the pandemic, a societal level, Boss told me.
sentences.zh: 博斯告诉我：“这是我第一次将模棱两可的失去提升到一个更高的层面，即关于大流行的社会层面。”

sentences.en: In trying to describe losses that society doesn't always recognize,
sentences.zh: 在试图描述社会并不总能认出的失去时，

sentences.en: Boss might be helping us to rethink the nature of loss altogether.
sentences.zh: 博斯可能正在帮助我们彻底重新思考失去的本质。

sentences.en: Boss emanates the wisdom of a lifetime spent focused on an idea.
sentences.zh: 博斯散发着将一生专注于一个理念所沉淀的智慧。

sentences.en: Her manner is thoughtful and serene.
sentences.zh: 她的举止沉思而宁静。

sentences.en: During our conversation, she chose her words carefully, gazing out the window while searching for the best possible formulation.
sentences.zh: 在我们的交谈中，她字斟句酌，凝视着窗外，寻找着最佳的表述方式。

sentences.en: Her work can be grim in nature, but she is quick to laugh and delights in small pleasures.
sentences.zh: 她的工作本质上可能是严峻的，但她总是爽朗地笑，并在细小的快乐中感到愉悦。

sentences.en: On her birthday, she was content to go for vanilla ice cream with chocolate chips.
sentences.zh: 在她的生日那天，她满足于去吃带有巧克力豆的香草冰淇淋。

sentences.en: Though her ouvre is vast, eight books, more than a hundred peer-reviewed articles and chapters,
sentences.zh: 尽管她的著作等身——八本书、一百多篇同行评审的文章和章节、

sentences.zh: 跨越大约44年的数千次引用，她在回答我的问题时，依然从一个保存完好的档案馆中汲取养分，轻松地讲述着几十年前的轶事和论点。

sentences.en: The daughter of a tenant farmer and a homemaker, Boss grew up in New Glarus, a Wisconsin village populated mostly by Swiss immigrants, including her father.
sentences.zh: 作为佃农和家庭主妇的女儿，博斯在威斯康星州的新格拉鲁斯长大，这是一个主要由瑞士移民（包括她的父亲）组成的村庄。

sentences.en: He came to the United States during the 1920s to study agriculture, intending to return to
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪20年代来到美国学习农业，本打算返回

sentences.en: Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 瑞士。

sentences.en: Then the Great Depression hit.
sentences.zh: 然后大萧条爆发了。

sentences.en: He was stuck.
sentences.zh: 他被困住了。

sentences.en: Eventually, Boss's father married and started a family in America, working with dairy cows and growing crops.
sentences.zh: 最终，波斯的父亲在美国结婚并组建了家庭，以养奶牛和种地为生。

sentences.en: He missed his home, but he wasn't sure that he could ever return.
sentences.zh: 他思念家乡，但又不确定自己是否还能回去。

sentences.en: Boss noticed he sometimes became distant, especially when letters arrived from
sentences.zh: 波斯发现他有时会变得疏离，尤其是当信件从

sentences.en: Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 瑞士寄来时。

sentences.en: Homesickness became a central part of my family's culture, Boss wrote in her 1999 book.
sentences.zh: “思乡之情成了我家文化的核心部分，”波斯在她1999年出版的书写道。

sentences.en: Longing for faraway family members was so common that at an early age, I became curious about this unnamed loss and the melancholy that never went away.
sentences.zh: 对远方亲人的渴望如此普遍，以至于我在很小的时候，就开始对这种无名失落感以及挥之不去的忧郁产生好奇。

sentences.en: It was all around me.
sentences.zh: 它无处不在。

sentences.en: In 1952, Boss started college in Madison.
sentences.zh: 1952年，波斯开始在麦迪逊上大学。

sentences.en: At the time, it was rare for a girl from her village to study beyond high school.
sentences.zh: 在当时，她村里的女孩读完高中后继续深造是很少见的。

sentences.en: Most married upon graduation, and Boss herself married as a 19-year-old college student.
sentences.zh: 大多数人在毕业时就结婚了，波斯本人也在19岁时作为一名女大学生结了婚。

sentences.en: Yet she was eager to learn about a world beyond the farmland of southern Wisconsin, where going out on the weekend meant a Friday night fish fry and dancing the polka.
sentences.zh: 然而，她渴望了解威斯康星州南部农田之外的世界，在那里，周末外出意味着周五晚上的炸鱼和跳波尔卡舞。

sentences.en: After college, she studied for a master's degree in child development and family studies,
sentences.zh: 大学毕业后，她攻读了儿童发展与家庭研究的硕士学位，

sentences.en: writing her thesis on the cultural roles across three generations of Swiss American and Amish women in her hometown.
sentences.zh: 她的硕士论文以家乡的三代瑞士裔美国人和阿米什女性的文化角色为主题。

sentences.en: Excited by this kitchen table research, in which anecdotal information gleaned from hours of conversation became the data, Boss embarked on an academic career that existed
sentences.zh: 受这种餐桌研究的启发，通过数小时对话收集到的轶事信息成了数据，波斯开启了一段学术生涯，

sentences.en: at the edge of disciplines in the relatively unknown field of family social science.
sentences.zh: 这段生涯游走于各个学科边缘，涉足相对陌生的家庭社会科学领域。

sentences.en: As a doctoral student in the early 1970s, she developed the theory for which she is best known.
sentences.zh: 20世纪70年代初，作为一名博士生，她提出了令她最负盛名的理论。

sentences.en: Invited to observe a psychiatrist's session at the university's family therapy clinic, she noticed that the fathers were always angry about being there.
sentences.zh: 应邀在大学家庭治疗诊所旁听一位精神病学家的会诊时，她注意到父亲们对来这里总是感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And they said, the children are mother's business.
sentences.zh: 他们说，孩子是母亲的事。

sentences.en: Why am I here, Boss told me.
sentences.zh: “我为什么会在这里？”波斯对我说。

sentences.en: The fathers, many of whom worked corporate jobs, were too preoccupied to help raise their children.
sentences.zh: 这些父亲们许多人从事公司的工作，整日忙得不可开交，无暇帮忙抚养孩子。

sentences.en: She termed the phenomenon psychological father absence in intact families.
sentences.zh: 她将这种现象称之为完整家庭中的心理学父亲缺席。

sentences.en: But a professor who taught her theory development course pushed her to think bigger.
sentences.zh: 但她的一位教授理论发展课程的教授促使她放宽眼光、思考更大格局。

sentences.en: In retrospect, Boss says, she could have spent the next decade writing solely about fathers.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，波斯说，她本可以把接下来的十年全用来写关于父亲的文章。

sentences.en: Instead, following her professor's advice, she landed on a broader research concept, ambiguous loss.
sentences.zh: 相反，遵照教授的建议，她最终选定了一个更广泛的研究概念——模棱两可的失落。

sentences.en: Her father's estrangement from his European family and his emotional absence from his American one were the germs of Boss's theory.
sentences.zh: 她父亲与欧洲家庭的疏离以及对美国家庭的情感缺席，正是波斯这一理论的萌芽。

sentences.en: She now knows that her father was experiencing ongoing grief in which no death had occurred.
sentences.zh: 她现在明白，她的父亲当时正在经历一种没有发生死亡的持续悲伤。

sentences.en: While she realized then that what she felt was the ambiguity, the loss was vague.
sentences.zh: 虽然她当时意识到她所感受到的是这种模棱两可，但这种失落感是模糊不清的。

sentences.en: Theorizing a category of loss would help Boss, fellow academics, and laypeople, make sense of griefs whose origins and parameters were equally unclear.
sentences.zh: 将这一类失落概念化，将有助于波斯、同行学者以及普通人理解那些起源和界限同样不清的悲伤。

sentences.en: Over the next 45 years, as a researcher and therapist, Boss worked with thousands of families who struggled with similar dynamics.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的45年里，作为一名研究人员和治疗师，波斯与成千上万面临类似家庭动力困境的家庭合作过。

sentences.en: Often, she was called to provide emergency therapy for people whose relatives were missing following a disaster.
sentences.zh: 通常，当灾难过后亲人失踪时，她会被请去为这些人提供紧急心理治疗。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, she was coping with her own personal tragedies, the deaths of both her parents and her sister.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，她也在应对自己的个人悲剧——双亲和姐姐相继离世。

sentences.en: Boss found that ambiguous loss can result in what she termed frozen grief, when people are stuck in their sorrow, or disenfranchised grief,
sentences.zh: 波斯发现，模棱两可的失落会导致她所谓的“冻结的悲伤”（人们深陷悲痛无法自拔），或是“剥夺权利的悲伤”，

sentences.zh: 这是一个由心理健康咨询师肯尼斯·J·

sentences.en: Doka to describe when others do not see a significant loss as legitimate or deserving of support.
sentences.zh: 多卡创造的术语，用于描述他人不认为重大的失落是合法的或值得支持的情况。

sentences.en: To that end, her work diverges from historical grief research, which has considered sorrow something to overcome.
sentences.zh: 为此，她的工作不同于以往将悲伤视为需要克服的事物的历史悲伤研究。

sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德的《哀悼与

sentences.en: response, and therapists following this model counseled their clients to let go of whomever they had loSt.
sentences.zh: 反应，遵循这一模式的治疗师建议他们的客户放下他们失去的任何人。

sentences.en: Such training focused on helping clients seek closure, an endpoint to grief.
sentences.zh: 这种训练侧重于帮助客户寻求完结（closure），即悲伤的终点。

sentences.en: Rejecting linear models, Boss offers six non-sequential guidelines meant to help people bear their grief.
sentences.zh: 波斯拒绝线性模型，提出了六条非线性的指导方针，旨在帮助人们承受悲伤。

sentences.en: Making meaning out of loss, relinquishing one's desire to control an uncontrollable situation, recreating identity after loss, becoming accustomed to ambivalent feelings,
sentences.zh: 从失落中赋予意义、放弃控制无法控制局面的渴望、在失落后重塑自我、习惯矛盾的情感、

sentences.en: redefining one's relationship with whatever or whomever they've lost, and finding new hope.
sentences.zh: 重新定义自己与所失去的任何事物或人的关系，以及寻找新的希望。

sentences.en: Two of the guidelines, meaning and new hope, are especially important for coping, intended to help
sentences.zh: 其中两项指导方针——意义和新的希望，对于应对困境尤为重要，旨在帮助

sentences.en: people consider what the loss signifies in their lives and how they can imagine a future that contains their loss.
sentences.zh: 人们思考失落在他们生活中意味着什么，以及他们如何构想一个包含失落在内的未来。

sentences.en: Boss draws from the work of thinkers who challenge the presumptions of linearity in the
sentences.zh: 波斯借鉴了一些思想家的著作，这些人挑战了悲伤过程中线性发展的假设，

sentences.en: grief process and provide language that breaks free from the confines of Freud's formal writings.
sentences.zh: 并提供了打破弗洛伊德正式著作束缚的语言。

sentences.en: She finds inspiration in the writings of Viktor Frankl, an Austrian psychotherapist and concentration camp
sentences.zh: 她从维克多·弗兰克的著作中获得灵感，维克多·弗兰克是一位奥地利心理治疗师兼集中营

sentences.en: survivor who wrote of searching for meaning in loss, and the psychologist Dennis Klass, whose theory of
sentences.zh: 幸存者，他写过在失落中寻找意义；她也从心理学家丹尼斯·克拉斯的理论中获得灵感，

sentences.en: continuing bonds offers a paradigm of bereavement in which mourners maintain a relationship, if only psychological, with the deceased.
sentences.zh: 其持续联结理论提供了一种悲恸范式，其中哀悼者与死者保持着一种关系，哪怕只是心理上的。

sentences.en: While simplistic declarations of closure are comforting for bystanders, they are hurtful for the bereaved, Boss writes.
sentences.zh: 波斯写道，虽然简单化的“完结”宣言能给旁观者带来安慰，但对哀悼者来说却是伤害。

sentences.en: If we have loved, we will want to remember.
sentences.zh: 如果我们爱过，我们就会想要记住。

I first encountered Boss's ideas in July 2020.
sentences.zh: 我于2020年7月首次接触到波斯的思想。

sentences.en: My grandfather had just died of COVID-19, which he contracted at his care facility near Dallas.
sentences.zh: 我的祖父刚刚死于COVID-19，他在达拉斯附近的疗养院感染了这种病毒。

sentences.en: My mother, brother, and I had driven halfway across the country to say goodbye to him through a closed window.
sentences.zh: 我母亲、兄弟和我开车横跨大半个国家，隔着紧闭的窗户跟他做最后的告别。

sentences.en: Because he had Alzheimer's, I had spent years trying to say goodbye.
sentences.zh: 因为他患有阿尔茨海默病，我花了好几年时间试图跟他告别。

sentences.en: But this final time was abrupt, ragged like a wound reopened.
sentences.zh: 但最后这一次却如此突兀，像一个重新撕裂的伤口一样鲜血淋漓。

sentences.en: We told him we loved him, and he struggled for air.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉他我们爱他，而他艰难地喘着气。

sentences.en: After two days of this, he died in the night.
sentences.zh: 经过两天的煎熬，他在夜里去世了。

sentences.en: One afternoon, about a week later, while waiting to pick up his ashes, I heard Boss on a 2016 episode of the podcast On Being.
sentences.zh: 大约一周后的一个下午，在等待领取他的骨灰时，我在播客《本真》2016年的一期节目中听到了波斯的声音。

sentences.en: Her voice, clear yet gentle, cut through the air conditioner's thrum as she spoke with Krista Tippett, the show's hoSt. We're not comfortable with unanswered questions, Boss said.
sentences.zh: 当她与该节目的主持人克丽斯塔·蒂佩特交谈时，她那清晰而温柔的声音穿透了空调的嗡嗡声。“我们对未解的问题感到不自在，”波斯说。

sentences.en: These are losses that are minus facts.
sentences.zh: “这些是没有事实依据的失落。”

sentences.en: I wasn't alone.
sentences.zh: 我并不孤单。

sentences.en: During the pandemic, Tippett noticed that people were posting on social media about that interview.
sentences.zh: 在大流行期间，蒂佩特注意到人们在社交媒体上发布关于那次采访的内容。

sentences.en: People were saying, I'm listening to this again.
sentences.zh: “人们在说：‘我又在听这个了。’

sentences.en: It's really helping me, Tippett said.
sentences.zh: ‘这真的帮了我大忙，’”蒂佩特说。

sentences.en: She decided to invite Boss back onto the show to discuss how her theory might apply to the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 她决定邀请波斯再次上节目，探讨她的理论如何应用于大流行。

sentences.en: They talked about losses, not just of life, but of livelihood, of possibility, of dreams, of plans, of things that seemed certain yesterday, Tippett told me.
sentences.zh: “他们谈论的失落，不仅仅是生命的失落，还有生计、可能性、梦想、计划以及昨天看来还很确定的事情的失落，”蒂佩特告诉我。

sentences.en: Boss had given me a theory for my own life, and language to describe the prolonged nature of my loss.
sentences.zh: 波斯为我自己的生活提供了一种理论，也提供了一种语言来描述我所经历的漫长失落。

sentences.en: For nearly a decade, my grandfather had succumbed to Alzheimer's until he could no longer remember my name or face.
sentences.zh: 近十年来，祖父一直被阿尔茨海默病折磨，直到他再也记不清我的名字或长相。

sentences.en: At the end of his life, we lived far apart, and that distance made it difficult to see him, a reality that now haunted me.
sentences.zh: 在他生命的尽头，我们天各一方，这种距离使得见他一面难上加难，这一现实如今一直萦绕在我心头。

sentences.en: There was a temporal lag in my experience of loss.
sentences.zh: 在我的失落体验中，存在着一种时间上的滞后。

sentences.en: Though he was now irrefutably gone, I'd been losing my grandfather for years.
sentences.zh: 尽管他现在已经千真万确地离去了，但我其实已经失去祖父好几年了。

sentences.en: His death dredged up old feelings of guilt and regret.
sentences.zh: 他的死勾起了我内心深处旧有的内疚和遗憾。

sentences.en: I mourned the time we never spent together, the questions I never asked.
sentences.zh: 我为我们从未一起度过的时间、我从未问出口的问题而感到哀伤。

sentences.en: Ambiguous loss seemed to explain this long, unsettled grief.
sentences.zh: 模棱两可的失落似乎解释了这种漫长而悬而未决的悲伤。

sentences.en: The myth of closure describes the complicated experience of mourning during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: “完结”的神话描述了在大流行期间哀悼的复杂经历。

sentences.en: To all of you who are grieving someone or something you loved and lost during this pandemic, may I say this?
sentences.zh: “对于你们所有在这场大流行中为所爱并失去的人或事物感到悲伤的人，请允许我这么说，”

sentences.en: Boss writes, it is not closure you need, but certainty that your loved one is gone.
sentences.zh: 波斯写道，“你需要的不是完结，而是确信你爱的人已经离去。

sentences.en: That they understood why you could not be there to comfort them.
sentences.zh: 确信他们理解为什么你当时无法去安慰他们。

sentences.en: That they loved you and forgave you in their last moments of life.
sentences.zh: 确信他们在生命的最后时刻爱着你并原谅了你。

sentences.en: Without these things, some doubts may linger for you, but that is the nature of loss.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这些，你可能会心存疑虑，但这正是失落的本质。

sentences.en: Its ending is never perfect, even in the best of times.
sentences.zh: 它的结局永远不会是完美的，即使在最好的时期也是如此。”

sentences.en: Boss intends for the book, a relatively slim text comprising nine chapters, to be therapeutic.
sentences.zh: 波斯希望这本书（一本包含九个章节的相对精炼的文本）能够具有治疗作用。

sentences.en: It's a hybrid work, a self-help book providing strategies for coping with ambiguous loss, but also a document of
sentences.zh: 这是一部混合作品，既是一本提供应对模棱两可失落策略的自助书，也是一份记录

sentences.en: observations from 40-plus years researching and counseling families, and a personal meditation on love and loss.
sentences.zh: 她40多年来研究和辅导家庭的观察文档，还是一篇关于爱与失落的个人沉思录。

sentences.en: While her old arguments against binary thinking in favor of accepting paradox are the foundation, the book is also a response to overwhelming global catastrophes of late.
sentences.zh: 虽然她反对二元思维、赞成接纳悖论的旧观点是基础，但这本书也是对近年全球压倒性灾难的回应。

sentences.en: This worldwide health crisis brought many ambiguous losses, she writes.
sentences.zh: 她写道：“这场全球健康危机带来了许多模棱两可的失落。”

sentences.en: Loved ones died alone in hospitals with no family allowed, all losing the comfort of a last goodbye.
sentences.zh: 挚爱之人独自在医院离去，不允许家人陪伴，所有人都失去了最后告别的安慰。

sentences.en: Students lost rituals of graduation and saying goodbye to classmates, as well as the chance to meet new friends at the beginning of a new academic year.
sentences.zh: 学生们失去了毕业典礼和跟同窗告别的仪式，也失去了清新学年伊始结识新朋友的机会。

sentences.en: Younger children were schooled at home, many alone in their rooms in front of a computer.
sentences.zh: 较小的孩子在家上学，许多人独自待在房间里的电脑前。

sentences.en: Others struggled because they had no broadband, computer, or internet access.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则因为没有宽带、电脑或互联网接入而举步维艰。

sentences.en: The critical experiences that traditionally marked growing up were lost, a surreal experience for the young as well as their parents.
sentences.zh: 传统上标志着成长的关键体验消失了，这对年轻人以及他们的父母来说都是一种超现实的体验。

sentences.en: Outlining why these losses are ambiguous, Boss considers the theory's two original categories, physical and psychological.
sentences.zh: 在概述为什么这些失落是模棱两可的时，波斯考虑了该理论最初的两个类别：生理上的和心理上的。

sentences.en: The first is physical, no body to bury, no proof of death.
sentences.zh: 第一种是生理上的，没有尸体可埋，没有死亡的证据。

sentences.en: We see this now with COVID-19 deaths, where families are not allowed to view the body or have the
sentences.zh: “我们现在在COVID-19的死亡中看到了这一点，当时家属不被允许瞻仰遗体，也不能举行

sentences.en: usual funeral rituals of mourning and burial, she writes, describing the pandemic's early days.
sentences.zh: 通常的哀悼和埋葬葬礼仪式，”她在描述大流行初期时写道。

sentences.en: Psychological absences can also include obsessions or preoccupations, she continues, noting that many people have been preoccupied with worry and anxiety about the virus.
sentences.zh: 她接着说：“心理上的缺席也可以包括痴迷或全神贯注，”她指出许多人一直全神贯注于对病毒的担忧和焦虑中。

sentences.en: Social distancing was also an ambiguous loss, she argues.
sentences.zh: 她认为，保持社交距离也是一种模棱两可的失落。

sentences.en: Unable to visit loved ones, we were psychologically present, but physically absent.
sentences.zh: 无法探望挚爱之人，我们在心理上在线，但在生理上缺席。

sentences.en: The theory is not as narrow as it was in the inception, a positive development, Boss told me, because more people can find the concept meaningful in their own lives.
sentences.zh: 波斯对我说，该理论并不像刚创立时那么狭隘，这是一个积极的发展，因为更多的人能在自己的生活中发现这个概念的意义。

sentences.en: Researchers have expanded the original two categories to include applications beyond the family.
sentences.zh: 研究人员已经将最初的两个类别进行了扩展，使其应用超出了家庭的范畴。

sentences.en: The theory of ambiguous loss has left my desk long ago, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说：“模棱两可的失落理论很久以前就已经离开我的办公桌了。”

sentences.en: While Boss cautions that ambiguous loss can't be a theory of everything, she also acknowledges that ambiguity is difficult to measure.
sentences.zh: 虽然波斯告诫说模棱两可的失落不能成为解释一切的理论，但她也承认这种模棱两可很难衡量。

sentences.en: It is perceptual in the person's mind, she told me, making its study particularly personal.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，这是人脑中的一种感知，这使得对它的研究变得格外个人化。

sentences.en: Social scientists like herself assess whether something may be considered an ambiguous loss based on qualitative interviews plus some quantitative data,
sentences.zh: 像她这样的社会科学家会根据定性访谈加上一些定量数据来评估某事是否可以被视为模棱两可的失落，

sentences.en: how interviewees describe their loss is a key indicator of whether it is ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 受访者如何描述他们的失落是判断其是否模棱两可的关键指标。

sentences.en: Boss gives examples of such language in her work.
sentences.zh: 波斯在她的著作中给出了这种语言的例子。

sentences.en: Am I married or not since my husband has been missing for decades?
sentences.zh: 既然我的丈夫已经失踪了几十年，我是结婚了还是没结婚？

sentences.en: How do I answer how many children I have when I gave one up for adoption?
sentences.zh: 当我把一个孩子送去收养时，我该如何回答我有几个孩子？

sentences.en: When asked to define the theory, Boss simply says it is an unclear loss that can be physical or psychological, and it has no resolution.
sentences.zh: 当被要求定义该理论时，波斯简单地表示，这是一种不明确的失落，可以是生理上的或心理上的，且没有解决方案。

sentences.en: Undergirding the idea are core assumptions that speak to its subjectivity, the first of which states that a phenomenon can exist even if it cannot be measured.
sentences.zh: 支撑这一思想的是指向其主观性的核心假设，其中第一条指出，一种现象即使无法被衡量也依然可以存在。

sentences.en: In other words, the loss's immeasurability doesn't negate its existence or its crippling effects.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，失落的不可衡量性并不否定它的存在或它那摧毁性的影响。

sentences.en: Second, she assumes that when it comes to ambiguous loss, there is no single narrative that can explain a deprivation.
sentences.zh: 其次，她假设，当谈到模棱两可的失落时，并没有单一的叙事可以解释这种剥夺感。

sentences.en: Subjectivity colors our perception of loss.
sentences.zh: 主观性为主我们对失落的感知涂上了色彩。

sentences.en: The goal of social scientists and therapists should be to determine how people can live well despite not knowing or understanding the scope of their loss.
sentences.zh: 社会科学家和治疗师的目标应该是弄清楚人们如何在不了解或不理解失落范围的情况下依然生活得很好。

sentences.en: Third, ambiguous loss is a relational phenomenon based on attachment.
sentences.zh: 第三，模棱两可的失落是一种基于依恋的关系现象。

sentences.en: That ambiguous loss is so broad may be frustrating to those who crave absolute parameters, but its haziness is the point.
sentences.zh: 模棱两可的失落如此广泛，对那些渴望绝对界限的人来说可能会令人沮丧，但它的模糊性正是关键所在。

sentences.en: It's a theory about imprecision, and how do those of us who like precision live with such ambiguity, Boss told me.
sentences.zh: 波斯告诉我：“这是一个关于不精准的理论，而我们这些喜欢精准的人该如何与这种模棱两可共存呢？”

sentences.en: If ambiguous loss seems to encompass an impossibly large field, it is because the researchers and writers following after Boss see its potential to reshape society's expectations
sentences.zh: 如果模棱两可的失落似乎涵盖了一个大得不可思议的领域，那是因为跟随波斯之后的研究人员和作家看到了它重塑社会对悲伤期盼的潜力。

sentences.en: for grief.
sentences.zh: 悲伤。

sentences.en: Last year, Boss received a flood of public and scholarly inquiries about one particular application of the theory—racism as ambiguous loss.
sentences.zh: 去年，波斯收到了大量关于该理论的一个特定应用的公众和学术咨询——即把种族主义视为模棱两可的失落。

sentences.en: In May 2020, George Floyd was murdered, just a few miles south of Boss's apartment.
sentences.zh: 2020年5月，乔治·弗洛伊德遇害，地点就在波斯公寓以南几英里处。

sentences.en: Younger scholars had already begun using her framework to research the extreme stresses of racism, and now, following their lead, Boss turned her attention to a loss pervasive in
sentences.zh: 年轻学者已经开始利用她的框架来研究种族主义带来的极端压力，现在，在他们的引领下，波斯将注意力转向了在她自己的城市中无处不在的失落。

sentences.en: her own city.
sentences.zh: 自己的城市。

sentences.en: In The Myth of Closure, Boss contributes to the already robust study of slavery's traumatic aftermath.
sentences.zh: 在《完结的神话》中，波斯为本已蓬勃发展的关于奴隶制创伤后遗症的研究做出了贡献。

sentences.en: She suggests that losses from slavery—the experience of being wrenched from home and family, of losing control over one's own body—were ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 她提出，来自奴隶制的失落——被强行剥离出家园和家庭的经历、对自身身体失去控制的经历——是模棱两可的。

sentences.en: These relationship ruptures—which, to me, recall the sociologist Orlando Patterson's theory that enslavement caused social death—produced
sentences.zh: 这些关系的破裂——在我看来，这让人想起社会学家奥兰多·帕特森的理论，即奴隶制导致了社会性死亡——产生了

sentences.en: a generational transmission of trauma, remembered today in the bodies and minds of their descendants, and omnipresent in the systems that continue to oppress black people today.
sentences.zh: 创伤的代际传递，如今在他们后代的身体和大脑中被铭记，并且在今天继续压迫黑人的系统中无处不在。

sentences.en: Boss draws from scholarship in family therapy, sociology, and social work, particularly the work of Elaine Pinderhughes, who,
sentences.zh: 波斯借鉴了家庭治疗、社会学和田野社会工作领域的学术成果，特别是伊莱恩·平德休斯的著作，

sentences.en: she writes, was one of the first to teach me that historical context matters for human development and
sentences.zh: 她写道，平德休斯是第一批教导她“历史背景对人类发展至关重要，

sentences.en: that being traumatized instead of nurtured will affect not only children but also their own offspring as well.
sentences.zh: 遭受创伤而非得到滋养不仅会影响儿童，还会影响他们自己的后代”的学者之一。

sentences.en: The harrowing video of George Floyd's murder catalyzed an intense outpouring of grief and anger, a manifestation of omnipresent racial trauma.
sentences.zh: 乔治·弗洛伊德遇害的惨烈视频引发了悲伤和愤怒的强烈宣泄，这是无处不在的种族创伤的一种显现。

sentences.en: That continual trauma, Boss suggests, is where ambiguous loss lies.
sentences.zh: 波斯认为，这种持续的创伤，正是模棱两可的失落所在之处。

sentences.en: Scholars have long studied racism as a source of stress and grief.
sentences.zh: 学者们长期以来一直将种族主义作为压力和悲伤的根源进行研究。

sentences.en: In the 1970s, the psychiatrist Chester Pierce wrote about the stressful, mundane, extreme environment in which black Americans live.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代，精神病学家切斯特·皮尔斯撰文论述了美国黑人生活在其中充满压力、平凡而极端的环境。

sentences.en: But now, family scientists are finding new resonance in Boss's work to explain how racism can produce ambiguous losses in black families and communities.
sentences.zh: 但现在，家庭科学家在波斯的工作中找到了新的共鸣，用以解释种族主义如何在黑人家庭和社区中产生模棱两可的失落。

sentences.en: One scholar applying the framework is
sentences.zh: 应用该框架的一位学者是

sentences.en: Shalandra Bryant, a professor of family social science at the University of Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 沙兰德拉·布莱恩特，明尼苏达大学家庭社会科学教授。

sentences.en: While researching marriage in black southern families in the mid-2000s, Bryant met a woman who confided that her husband was acting unusually withdrawn.
sentences.zh: 在2000年代中期研究美国南部黑人家庭的婚姻状况时，布莱恩特遇到了一位女性，她倾诉说自己的丈夫表现得异常冷漠。

sentences.en: Although he was still functioning, going to work, picking up his child from school, he was emotionally vacant.
sentences.zh: 尽管他仍在正常生活、去上班、接孩子放学，但在情感上他却是一片空白。

sentences.en: Bryant learned that news reports about racist incidents and his child's experiences in school had deeply affected him.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩特了解到，有关种族主义事件的新闻报道以及他的孩子在学校的经历对他产生了深远的影响。

sentences.en: It turns out that he was depressed and apprehensive and he couldn't quite put his finger on why, Bryant said.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩特说，事实证明，他感到沮丧和焦虑，却又说不出个所以然。

sentences.en: He felt he had no control over making sure that his family felt safe.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己无法确保家人感受到安全。

sentences.en: Bryant sees Boss's theory as important to understanding the effects of stressors.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩特认为，博斯的理论对于理解压力源的影响至关重要。

sentences.en: Racism, she says, is a stressor impacting the lives of black Americans.
sentences.zh: 她说，种族主义是一个影响美国黑人生活的压力源。

sentences.en: That could leave a culture wondering, where do I fit here?
sentences.zh: 这可能会让一种文化不禁疑惑：我们在这个社会中究竟属于哪里？

sentences.en: Who are we as a culture that so many people can feel such hatred toward us?
sentences.zh: 作为一种文化，我们究竟是谁，为什么这么多人会对我们怀有如此深的恨意？

sentences.en: Bryant, who is black, said, I think that can make people wonder or think about where they fit in society.
sentences.zh: 身为黑人的布莱恩特说：“我认为这会让人不禁疑惑或思考，他们在社会中到底处于什么位置。”

sentences.en: Today, Bryant is working with a team on a project that examines financial strain on black families through the lens of Boss's theory.
sentences.zh: 如今，布莱恩特正与一个团队合作开展一个项目，通过博斯的理论视角来审视黑人家庭所承受的财务压力。

sentences.en: Racist housing policies historically prevented black Minneapolis residents from accumulating wealth.
sentences.zh: 历史上，奉行种族主义的住房政策阻碍了明尼阿波利斯的黑人居民积累财富。

sentences.en: Today, only 25 percent own homes in the metropolitan area.
sentences.zh: 如今，大都市区只有25%的黑人拥有自己的住房。

sentences.en: compared with 77 percent of white residents, the largest home ownership gap of any major American city.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，白人居民的这一比例为77%，这是美国所有主要城市中最大的住房自有率差距。

sentences.en: Financial stress, Bryant says, can contribute to people losing their sense of self, often without understanding why.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩特说，经济压力会导致人们失去自我意识，而且往往弄不清原因。

sentences.en: In this way, the nebulous effects of anti-black racism permeate the psyche.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，反黑人种族主义那捉摸不透的影响渗透到了心灵深处。

sentences.en: In mid-July, I returned to Minneapolis and asked Boss to accompany me to the intersection of 38th Street and Chicago
sentences.zh: 七月中旬，我重返明尼阿波利斯，并请博斯陪我前往38街与芝加哥大道的交汇处

sentences.en: Avenue, known as George Floyd Square.
sentences.zh: 也就是被称为乔治·弗洛伊德广场的地方。

sentences.en: In May, the intersection was closed to traffic, inviting mourning, meditation, and proteSt. Now, I saw that the offerings and gardens previously
sentences.zh: 今年五月，这个路口对交通关闭，成了人们悼念、冥思和抗议的地方。现在我看到，先前占据那片空间的供品和花园

sentences.en: occupying the space were moved to make room for cars.
sentences.zh: 已经被移走，好为汽车腾出地方。

sentences.en: A silhouette of Floyd, face down with wings sprouting from his shoulders, marking the spot where the police officer Derek Chauvin knelt on his neck,
sentences.zh: 一幅弗洛伊德的剪影趴在地上，肩膀上长着翅膀，标记着那名警察德里克·沙文用膝盖压住他脖子的位置。

sentences.en: was now surrounded by concrete barriers to protect against traffic.
sentences.zh: 周围现在围上了混凝土路障，以防车辆通行。

sentences.en: We ran into a man named Jay Webb, a volunteer gardener.
sentences.zh: 我们偶遇了一位名叫杰伊·韦布的男子，他是一名志愿园丁。

sentences.en: He cried out when he learned Boss's name.
sentences.zh: 当得知博斯的名字时，他惊呼出声。

sentences.en: Your line of thinking has helped me, he said excitedly, rushing to grab his phone for a selfie.
sentences.zh: “你的思想指引了我，”他兴奋地说着，赶忙抓起手机想要自拍。

sentences.en: Webb said he encourages visitors to accept their grief and search for peace, sentiments that echoed Boss's thought.
sentences.zh: 韦布说，他鼓励游客们接受悲伤、寻找平静，这些看法与博斯的思想不谋而合。

sentences.en: It was clear her work had expanded into the public sphere, moving people in her own city.
sentences.zh: 很显然，她的学术工作已经扩展到公共领域，触动了她所在城市的居民。

sentences.en: Webb told Boss, you are so, so needed here.
sentences.zh: 韦布对博斯说：“这里真的、真的很需要你。”

sentences.en: The theory of ambiguous loss originated in the families and communities she studied and counseled decades ago, and encounters with everyday people like
sentences.zh: 模糊性失落理论源于她几十年前研究和辅导的家庭与社区，而与韦布这样的普通人的相遇

sentences.en: Webb continue to shape her thinking.
sentences.zh: 一直在塑造着她的思想。

sentences.en: Boss, who considers herself a lifelong student, learns from these people.
sentences.zh: 自视为终身学习者的博斯，正向这些人虚心学习。

sentences.en: I need to keep my eyes open, Boss told me, after we visited George Floyd Square.
sentences.zh: “我需要保持清醒的头脑，”博斯在参观完乔治·弗洛伊德广场后对我说。

sentences.en: She recognizes the limits of her knowledge, and expresses gratitude for people who, even in the twilight of her career, have pushed those limits.
sentences.zh: 她认识到自己知识的局限性，并对那些即使在她职业生涯的暮年依然不断挑战这些局限的人心存感激。

sentences.en: With the myth of closure, Boss is learning in public.
sentences.zh: 带着关于释怀的虚幻迷思，博斯正在公众的目光下不断学习。

sentences.en: The resulting book emerged from reflection during the first months of the pandemic as a response to what was happening around me at the time, she says.
sentences.zh: 她说，这本著作源于大流行头几个月的反思，是对当时我身边所发生事情的回应。

sentences.en: I realized that not only was I changing, but that the people who were writing to me were
sentences.zh: 她对我说：“我意识到不仅我在改变，那些写信给我的人们

sentences.en: writing about different things, she told me, which stimulated my own rethinking, new thinking.
sentences.zh: 也在谈论不同的事情，这激发了我自己的反思和全新的思考。”

sentences.en: And though she is an expert on loss, Boss is herself learning how to grieve.
sentences.zh: 尽管她是失落研究领域的专家，但博斯自己也正在学习如何去经历悲痛。

sentences.en: In the summer of 2020, her husband's health took a turn for the worse.
sentences.zh: 2020年夏天，她丈夫的健康状况急转直下。

sentences.en: First, he was hospitalized.
sentences.zh: 起初，他住院了。

sentences.en: Then, a few weeks later, he was transferred to a rehabilitation facility.
sentences.zh: 接着，几周后，他被转到了康复中心。

sentences.en: One evening, Boss noticed her husband couldn't pick up his spoon, so she fed him instead.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，博斯发现丈夫连汤匙都拿不起来，于是改由她来喂他吃饭。

sentences.en: But he seemed his normal, genial self, and a nurse said he was improving.
sentences.zh: 但他看起来和往常一样温和，护士说他的情况正在好转。

sentences.en: Boss left for the evening.
sentences.zh: 博斯便离开回家过夜。

sentences.en: He blew her a kiss goodbye.
sentences.zh: 他隔空向她飞吻告别。

sentences.en: At 10 that night, a doctor called.
sentences.zh: 当晚10点，医生打来电话。

sentences.en: Her husband was unresponsive.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫已经没有了反应。

sentences.en: Boss and her daughter rushed to the facility, and there they learned he'd had a stroke.
sentences.zh: 博斯和女儿匆忙赶往康复中心，在那里得知他中风了。

sentences.en: The staff brought them chairs to rest, but they couldn't sleep.
sentences.zh: 工作人员搬来椅子让他们休息，但他们根本睡不着。

sentences.en: In the morning, Boss's daughter left to take a shower at home, and when she returned, suggested that her mother do the same.
sentences.zh: 清晨，博斯的女儿回家洗澡，回来后建议她的母亲也回去洗个澡。

sentences.en: Boss, however, said she would stay.
sentences.zh: 然而，博斯说她要留下来。

sentences.en: Everybody in my life, my father, my mother, my sister, my brother, died when I turned my back and left, Boss told me, her voice wavering.
sentences.zh: 博斯声音颤抖地对我说：“我生命中的所有人，我的父亲、母亲、姐姐、兄弟，都在我转身离开的时候离我而去。”

sentences.en: A heaviness settled over our conversation.
sentences.zh: 沉重的气氛笼罩了我们的交谈。

sentences.en: And I said, I'm not leaving.
sentences.zh: “当时我说：‘我不走。’”

sentences.en: And then I looked at him.
sentences.zh: “然后我看着他。”

sentences.en: And within about five minutes,
sentences.zh: “大约五分钟之内，”

sentences.en: he took his last breath.
sentences.zh: “他咽下了最后一口气。”

sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台受到严密掌控的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
